section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Chukas-Balak,
12 Tammuz*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "You have given a banner to those who fear You" applies to every Jew, because the attribute of Avraham's truth exists within each one.
section.t: "You have given a banner to those who fear You, to be raised high, because of the truth. Selah."
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe of the redemption and joy, brings in his maamar
(beginning with the words "Zeh" [this])
the explanation of Targum Yonasan: "You have given to those who fear You a miracle to be tested by it"
(from the word "nisayon" [test/trial])
"because of the truth of Avraham for all worlds."
And behold, this verse was said by Dovid, the sweet singer of Israel,
about each and every Jew.
From this it is understood
that all the details in this verse also exist in each and every Jew.
And it is also understood from the explanation of the Targum that "because of the truth. Selah" means "the truth of Avraham,"
and it is known
that the aspect of the Patriarchs exists within each and every person,
for we call only three "Patriarchs,"
"the Head of the rocks," etc.,
and especially Avraham, who is the first of the Patriarchs.
And from this it is understood that also what is stated, "You have given to those who fear You," etc.
(and the reason for this is "because of the truth. Selah")
also applies to each and every Jew,
as it is written,
"And now, Israel, what does the L-rd your G-d ask of you, but to fear," etc.,
for regarding the aspect of Moshe within each and every person, fear is a
small matter.
And it can be said that therefore each and every Jew,
even one who is called by the name "Israel,"
is called "those who fear You."
And this is what is said: "You have given a banner to those who fear You, to be raised high, because of the truth. Selah,"
that the Holy One, blessed be He, gives to each and every Jew a miracle to be raised high
(from the word "nisayon" [test/trial]),
because within each and every Jew there is the truth of Avraham.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the service of trials is specifically connected to Avraham because he opened the channel of self-sacrifice, which is the level of the Yechidah in the soul, and this is the inner meaning of "a miracle within a miracle."
section.t: B)
And he continues in the maamar,
And it is known that Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, opened the channel
of self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh).
And it can be said that with this he explains the reason why the service of trials is specifically connected with the truth of Avraham.
For at first glance, the primary service of Avraham was not in the matter of "those who fear You,"
the service of fear,
but rather in love, as it is written,
"Avraham, who loves Me."
To this he explains that Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, opened the channel of self-sacrifice,
that the service of trials is specifically through self-sacrifice,
for self-sacrifice is the perfection of the matter of fear and self-nullification.
And this is what is written,
"After the trial of the Binding, 'Now I know that you are a G-d-fearing person.'"
And behold, this that the service of trials is specifically through self-sacrifice,
the intention here is regarding the supernal level of it.
For, behold, the entirety of the service of Torah and mitzvos must be founded upon the service of self-sacrifice,
as it is stated in Tanya,

the reason why Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, commanded the generation that entered the Land to recite the Shema, etc., is because the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos depends on remembering the matter of self-sacrifice, etc.,
and likewise, the entire engagement in Torah and mitzvos and prayer for the soul is a matter of self-sacrifice, etc., since it does not contemplate the needs of the body, etc.,
but nevertheless, his service in a revealed way is not a matter of self-sacrifice,
but rather the service of Torah and mitzvos,
that he fulfills the positive commandments in all their details and is careful with the negative commandments in all their details,
from which it is understood that this is not the service of self-sacrifice as it is in itself,
but rather as it is connected with the service of Torah and mitzvos and is clothed within it,
which is service according to the order of the intellect and emotions.
And it can be said that in the powers of the soul, this is the matter of service from the aspect of the proximate encompassing light that relates to the internal and is clothed within it,
in the manner of the power of will that is clothed in wisdom,
and through it in the entirety of the power of intellect and emotions,
the internal powers of man,
in contrast, the service of trials is through the service of self-sacrifice itself,
and what devolves from this in matters of service in the ten powers of his soul is in the manner of a secondary matter and a result of its essential matter,
which is the matter of self-sacrifice.
And it can be said that in the powers of the soul, this is the aspect of the distant encompassing light,
the aspect of Yechidah in the soul.
And based on this, we can connect the two interpretations in the verse "You have given... a banner to be raised high,"
one, the matter of trials, as per the explanation of Targum Yonasan
(as above),
two, the matter of miracles,
and "a banner to be raised high" is
(in the manner of the language of our Sages, of blessed memory)
"a miracle within a miracle,"
because the service of trials is from the aspect of the level of "a miracle within a miracle" in the soul,
the aspect of Yechidah.
